subject.title: [Feature]: Improve `openclaw config` to avoid secrets and invalid files

question: Should bare interactive `openclaw config` change from the documented configure wizard to help output on already configured systems, and should literal writes to registry-known secret config paths warn or fail in favor of SecretRefs?
rationale: The remaining behavior crosses CLI compatibility and credential-safety policy; current docs and tests intentionally preserve the wizard path while current config set still supports direct value mode.

options.title: Add narrow guardrails
options.body: Show help for bare `openclaw config` on already configured systems while preserving `openclaw configure` and `--section`, and warn or fail only for registry-known secret literal writes with a clear SecretRef path.

options.title: Keep current contract
options.body: Leave bare `openclaw config` as the wizard and rely on docs, `config validate`, SecretRef builders, dry-run checks, and placeholder restoration for safer operation.

options.title: Go strict SecretRef-first
options.body: Fail closed for literal writes to supported secret targets, accepting stronger secret hygiene with higher compatibility impact for scripts and manual edits.

recommendation.title: Add narrow guardrails
recommendation.body: Show help for bare `openclaw config` on already configured systems while preserving `openclaw configure` and `--section`, and warn or fail only for registry-known secret literal writes with a clear SecretRef path.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision centers on the config CLI entrypoint and public setup contract, where this account has the clearest recent shared-runner history and prior review context.
